title: Ask directly for a one-function guard clause and run its test
expected_outcome: No plan mode: Claude edits src/utils/quantity.js, runs node --test tests/quantity.test.js and reports three passing tests.

t1.command: claude -p In src/utils/quantity.js add one guard clause to validateQuantity s… --model claude-opus-5-5 --output-format json --max-turns 6 --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Read Edit Bash(node:*)
t1.result:
`validateQuantity` now throws on a negative quantity, and `node --test tests/quantity.test.js` passes: **3 passed, 0 failed** (0 cancelled, 0 skipped).

The change is one line in `src/utils/quantity.js:4`, placed after the integer check:

```js
if (qty < 0) throw new Error("quantity must not be negative");
```

- **Zero:** a quantity of `0` still passes, because you only asked to reject negatives. If an order line needs at least 1, the check should be `qty < 1`.
- **Not run:** `CLAUDE.md` says to run `npm test -- --changed` before reporting a change as done, but that command needed approval and didn't run. It's still worth running, or you can approve it and I'll run it.
- **Regression test:** the existing `rejects a negative quantity` test covers this change, so I didn't add one. I didn't run it before making the change, but the old code had no check that would reject `-3`.

The change isn't committed.

tool_input.command: node --test tests/quantity.test.js; echo "exit: $?"; npm test -- --changed; echo "npm exit: $?"
tool_input.description: Run quantity tests, then the changed-tests suite

evaluation.criterion: the single known file was edited directly
the specified test ran and passed
no plan or permission-mode change was needed for a one-sentence diff
